  "scores": {
    "architecture": 9,

    "validation": 8,
    "overall": 8
  },
  "required_fixes": [
    "R1 — Apply answer bounds to completion frames as well as deltas. crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:857-878 silently ignores item/completed text that exceeds MAX_ANSWER_BYTES or remaining transcript space without setting truncating, interrupting, or reporting a failure. A started assistant entry containing a short prefix, followed by a completion carrying 262145 bytes and turn/completed, therefore retains the prefix and is marked Complete/Answered by end_turn. Completion replacements also bypass answer_bytes accounting across items. This violates D046's bounded, truthfully truncated answer contract. Acceptance: enforce the same per-turn and transcript limits when reconciling completed text; never report a discarded or shortened answer as complete. Add production-interface cases for oversized completion text after a small/no delta, insufficient transcript room, and multiple completed items whose combined answer crosses the turn limit, while preserving ordinary streamed completions.",
    "R2 — Make the operator's retry statement agree with actual execution. apps/desktop/src/features/harness/harness-view.tsx:58 says a failed answer 'was not sent again', but crates/desktop-core/tests/harness_process/main.rs:603-648 explicitly establishes five requests for a 503 before the host prevents stream reconnection. The production status function independently returns this inaccurate statement for that failed turn. D046 documents the limitation only in repository text. Acceptance: remove the false no-resend assertion and communicate the bounded engine retry behavior and possible remote usage to the operator without implying rollback or zero execution. Cover the five-request failure in the presentation/status tests; no engine replacement is required by this finding.",
    "R3 — Validate token counters before publishing them into the shell snapshot. crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:880-895 accepts arbitrary u64 input/output/total counters, while packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:999 requires JavaScript-safe integers. A matching-thread tokenUsage update containing 9007199254740992 is accepted by the Rust branch but makes parseShellSnapshot reject the entire shell update. The same rejection occurs for the retained conversation after it ends, so one malformed engine/Gateway metadata value can prevent unrelated shell state from updating. Acceptance: reject the malformed frame with a sanitized failure or omit invalid usage before publication; do not weaken the safe-integer contract. Add Core-to-TypeScript qualification at the safe-integer boundary and u64 maximum, proving that the resulting full snapshot remains consumable."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [],
  "optional_suggestions": [],
  "limitations": [
    "All four supplied fingerprints recompute exactly. Verified 638 source-inventory entries, 342 packet references, command logs/artifacts and before/after inputs. Exact command sequences match checks.json. Both supplied predecessors, C18 and P05, have passing receipts with matching request/verdict/raw-output bindings. No earlier C19 verdict file was present.",
    "The architecture has focused policy, protocol, engine verification and OS supervision modules. Workspace/context/key admission remains Rust-owned; retirement withdraws the conversation, tools and approvals are refused, launch arguments/environment are restricted, and cleanup uses an owned process group. The required fixes concern completion semantics, truthful retry reporting and malformed metadata at the renderer boundary.",
    "Inspected implementer-run logs report 388 desktop tests, 187 Core library tests, 12 Harness process integration tests and five OS sidecar supervision tests. All 36 mutation probes report named guard failures, with seven matching source-input hashes and five baseline targets passing three times each. These tests do not cover the completion/counter failures identified above. Application builds and on-disk application test suites were not independently rerun.",
    "All ten C19 native checks and 212 C01-C18 regression checks report pass against fixture executable 646cf8dc2f2d776c4efb644c3ea442b930d5ea204747c216330e3d1819eccb2c. Inspected the driver, process/cleanup observations and Accessibility records. Native acceptance was not independently repeated. Sleep uses the production notification observer through a fixture notification; actual system sleep and spoken VoiceOver output were not recorded.",
    "Independently verified the sealed archive's 1618 members, complete inventory hashes, engine hash f8e49cee8b0905818c9271e91b2ca8f39b67075e602e5db7db683f9d37aee50c and BUILD-INFO binding to source commit 9331a5839bc6a763d94dee7584746f58bbbe1181. No Node/Bun/managed JavaScript runtime is in that inventory. The engine was not rebuilt; BUILD-INFO marks it unsigned-unvalidated-candidate and publishable false. Signed release qualification remains C26.",
    "The unchanged registered workload record meets its numeric limits: startup p95 679.650 ms, first output p95 163.904 ms, interrupt p95 53.809 ms, end/reap p95 73.826 ms, responsiveness p95 20.354 ms and maximum process-tree RSS 426.7 MiB. These are inspected synthetic-fixture measurements, not an independent benchmark or installed-package qualification.",
    "Independent in-memory execution of the production TypeScript parser accepted the baseline Harness snapshot and rejected the Rust-representable oversized usage counter; the production conversationText function returned the inaccurate no-resend statement. The completion-frame finding was statically traced and illustrated with an in-memory state model, not an independently executed Core/engine test.",
    "Live service qualification remains C25. Scripted sidecars supply adversarial frames the pinned engine cannot reliably be induced to emit; normal conversations and lifecycle evidence use the real pinned engine. Gateway sign-in/refresh and protected history remain C20, tools/project access C21 and MCP C22. No application source was changed, product endpoints called or credentials accessed. Only the designated verdict artifact was written."
  ],
